revenue.title: Revenue & YoY Growth
revenue.content:
Group revenue across both segments, NZD millions.

For Skellerup: FY2026 revenue of $390.1m marks ten consecutive years of growth, up from $211.4m in FY2016 (~6.3% ten-year CAGR). Growth has been steadier than glamorous — no single year above ~11% — reflecting a mix of new-product wins, price and modest FX tailwind rather than acquisitions.

What to watch:

  • Whether North America (now ~38-40% of revenue) keeps growing given tariff uncertainty
  • Fonterra's 2026/27 milk price cut to $9.25/kgMS as a lead indicator for Agri demand
  • Industrial construction/roofing cyclicality in Australasia (soft) vs UK/US (strong)

ebitMargin.title: EBIT Margin Expansion
ebitMargin.content:
Operating (EBIT) margin, calculated on group revenue.

For Skellerup: this is the crux of the valuation debate. EBIT margin has expanded from 15.6% in FY2017 to an all-time high of 22.9% in FY2026 — a 7.3 percentage-point gain that accounts for most of the gap between Skellerup's 6.3% ten-year revenue CAGR and its 11.7% ten-year EBIT CAGR. That expansion is real (specification lock-in, new-product cadence, disciplined cost control) but management itself cautions 'these record results cannot continue ad infinitum.' The DCF's base case fades EBITDA margin from ~27% toward a still-excellent 25.5% mid-cycle level rather than extrapolating further expansion.

What to watch:

  • Whether margin holds at 22.9% or begins to mean-revert
  • Segment mix shift — Agri runs ~31% EBIT margin vs Industrial's ~22%, so faster Agri growth alone lifts the blended margin
  • Raw material/freight inflation and tariff costs, both explicitly cited as margin pressure

niVsFcf.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow
niVsFcf.content:
Statutory net income against free cash flow (operating cash flow less capex).

For Skellerup: FCF has consistently tracked or exceeded net income, evidence of clean, low-capex-intensity earnings (capex has typically run under $10m/yr, though FY2026 capex stepped up to $15.1m partly to replace the Wigram continuous-vulcanisation line damaged in the August 2025 fire). FY2026 statutory net income of $67.7m includes a non-recurring ~$4.8m pre-tax insurance gain related to that fire; normalised NPAT was $64.2m and should be used for any run-rate comparison.

What to watch:

  • Capex staying elevated into FY2027 as the CV-line replacement completes
  • Working capital discipline — the FY2026 OCF of $83.6m was almost exactly normalised NPAT plus D&A, i.e. no working-capital windfall inflating the base

epsDps.title: EPS vs Dividend per Share
epsDps.content:
Earnings and dividends per share, both in CENTS.

For Skellerup: a long, consistent dividend record — FY2026 DPS of 30.0 cents (+18% YoY) against EPS of 32.8 cents, a payout ratio near 90%. Because so much of earnings is distributed rather than retained, book equity grows slowly; this is a high-payout compounder, not a book-value compounder, which is why the DCF anchors forward growth to the revenue CAGR rather than the equity CAGR.

What to watch:

  • Payout ratio sustainability if earnings growth slows
  • EPS/DPS figures are in CENTS — do not divide the NZ$7.48 share price by 32.8 (that gives a meaningless 0.23x)

cashFlow.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Capex
cashFlow.content:
Cash generated from operations against capital expenditure.

For Skellerup: a capital-light business — capex has typically run 3-4% of revenue. FY2026 capex of $15.1m (vs $9.2m FY2025) is a step-up, largely the replacement continuous-vulcanisation line at the Wigram (Christchurch) plant following the August 2025 fire, guided to complete by end of FY2027. Even with the step-up, OCF of $83.6m comfortably covers capex and the dividend.

What to watch:

  • Capex normalising back toward the historical sub-$10m run-rate once the CV line is commissioned
  • Whether elevated capex recurs from further capacity investment or bolt-on M&A

netDebt.title: Net Debt
netDebt.content:
Total debt and cash on the balance sheet.

For Skellerup: net debt has fallen from $46.2m at FY2019 to a disclosed $2.0m at FY2026 year-end — an effectively unlevered balance sheet against a $55m syndicated facility (ANZ/ASB, expiring August 2028). FY2026 balance-sheet columns are NULL here because this row is sourced from the 19-Aug-2026 results release, not yet a published annual report; the net debt figure itself is the company's own disclosed number.

What to watch:

  • How management deploys the balance-sheet capacity — further capex, bolt-on M&A, or extra capital return
  • The FY2026 annual report, when published, will backfill equity/debt/cash detail
